t: If any individual rendering professional services on behalf of a professional corporation assumes a public office which prohibits his rendering of the professional services, or for any other reason is disqualified by law to render the professional services, he immediately shall sever all employment relationship in which he shares in the corporation’s profits attributable to professional services rendered after such assumption of office or other disqualification. For the purposes of section 16 of this Act, he shall be referred to as a “disqualified shareholder”.

fable.w: The section regulates private conduct: a professional who takes a public office or is otherwise legally disqualified must sever profit-sharing employment ties with a professional corporation and is termed a disqualified shareholder. The tempting reading is that "assumes a public office" signals government involvement, but no federal decision is being made and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue. There is no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or consultation.
fable.s: he immediately shall sever all employment relationship

qwen_block.w: This section defines the consequences for an individual who assumes public office or becomes disqualified from rendering professional services. It mandates that such an individual sever their employment relationship with a professional corporation. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The text deals with corporate governance and employment status relative to public office, not public participation in federal policy.
qwen_block.s: If any individual rendering professional services on behalf of a professional corporation assumes a public office which prohibits his rendering of the professional services, or for any other reason is disqualified by law to render the professional services, he immediately shall sever all employment relationship in which he shares in the corporation’s profits attributable to professional services rendered after such assumption of office or other disqualification.

opus.w: This section only requires a professional who takes a public office, or is otherwise disqualified, to end any arrangement in which he shares the corporation's profits. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue over any federal decision. The mention of a "public office" refers to the individual's new position, not to anyone outside the government taking part in a government decision.
opus.b: **Step 1: Analysis.** The section mentions a "public office" and a "disqualified shareholder," which could look like government involvement. That reading fails because the provision only says when a professional must cut financial ties with a professional corporation. No federal decision is being made, and nobody is consulted, heard, or given a chance to comment, advise, or sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines a 'disqualified shareholder' and mandates that such an individual sever employment relationships if they assume a public office or are otherwise disqualified by law. It does not require the federal government to consult with any outside party, nor does it involve outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The reference to 'public office' describes a condition for the individual, not a participatory mechanism for the government.
